text: The capacity forecast is read per owning service: each driver on Inputs, Monthly, Five years and Route activity belongs to exactly one service, and the per-service volume is that driver taken by formula, so the totals of the forecast do not move and no driver is split between two services.
why: Arch v5 splits Recovery into 19 services with their own topic and queue, so a capacity plan that stays at the Workbench level cannot size a service; taking the driver by formula keeps every existing figure intact.

applied_in: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Volume and Scale Forecast v4.xlsx, sheet Service volumes, rows 5 to 23
confirm: Data architecture team confirms which service owns each driver at the wave 1 gate.
impact: Every service gets a volume row with a basis cell; Inputs, Monthly, Five years and Route activity keep every value and formula.

text: Only rwb-source-data holds the grant on the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views and reads them on behalf of a screen or a workflow; every other service asks it, so a view read is a P1 SELECT and never a read by the whole Workbench or by a lake refresh.
why: Arch v5 gives the 30 views to rwb-source-data alone and makes the ACE read a contract call, so a document that names the Workbench or a lake refresh as the reader contradicts the architecture.

applied_in: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Volume and Scale Forecast v4.xlsx, Read path!A2, Read path!C16, Inputs!G7 and Key!C10
confirm: P1 owner confirms GET /freshness and the snapshot(page) result carry the reads the screens need.
impact: The read path keeps its figures; the reader is named as one service and no other service holds a view grant.

text: The three scheduled Workbench jobs of v3 become case creation and allocation (JOB-02 and JOB-03), reconciliation (JOB-04) and the WIN notice file (JOB-10); the lake refresh is retired with the lake and no Quartz job runs inside Recovery.
why: Arch v5 removes the data lake, retires the shared Quartz tables and runs each job in its owning service, so a lake refresh has no target and the count of three needs three real replacements.
read: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 line 513, line 2296 and lines 2978 to 3002; DP-10; DP-17; ADR-016.
applied_in: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Volume and Scale Forecast v4.xlsx, Read path!C15
confirm: Solution architecture team confirms the three named jobs at the wave 1 gate.
impact: The cell changes; B15 stays 3 and no other read-path figure moves. JOB-05 and the lake copy are dropped from the plan.

text: Every topic is rwb.<name>.events.v1 with 12 partitions, replication factor 3, seven-day retention, key caseId, CloudEvents 1.0 binary envelope, retry after 1 min, 10 min and 1 h and a .dlt topic; every service polls one task queue rwb-<name> in namespace rwb-recovery, and the decision record uses the shared topic rwb.decision-record.v1.
why: The forecast has no messaging content at all, so the settings can only come from the architecture; taking them once for all 19 services keeps the new sheet consistent with the topic library and the AC.

impact: 20 topic rows and 19 queue rows are added; ReportPublished, FileDelivered and FileFailed carry a named consumer or the placeholder.

text: Where the source counts no demand for a service, the sheet carries the placeholder and states the cadence it does know (one run per business day for payment matching and booking, per lot for debt sale, one screening per new case for deviation) instead of a derived number.
why: A capacity figure that the source does not hold would be invented; the cadence is stated in the architecture and is enough to size a queue and a worker pool until the volume is measured.

impact: Two cells carry the placeholder and four basis notes state what is missing; no figure is invented and no total changes.

text: The forecast keeps its own case inflow (new accounts divided by the accounts-per-case assumption of 1.2) and cites the Arch v5 slide 48 figure of 3,110 new cases a month beside it; no formula and no figure on Monthly or Five years is changed.
why: The forecast is the one artefact that holds the drivers and the assumption, and a document that silently swaps its inflow would break its own arithmetic; the conflict is recorded instead, in line with the rule that no number is invented or quietly replaced.

text: The three scheduled jobs of v3 are read as the Workbench-side jobs only, not as the whole platform job map; the number three is kept and the 21-job map of Arch v5 stays with the Batch and Scheduling and Temporal catalogues.
why: The two counts answer different questions and the source does not name its scope; keeping three as the Workbench-side count preserves the source while the job map lives in its own document.
